title: What If a Fish Was Hauled Up From the Deep Too Fast?
subject: fish underwater

scenes.text: What if a fish was pulled up from the deep too fast? Its own body turns on it.
Water pressure drops as it rises, and the gas inside the fish expands. Most cases start below about 30 feet.
The swim bladder swells like a balloon, and gas bubbles form under the scales.
The stomach can be pushed out through the mouth, and the eyes bulge outward.
Bubbles can even form in the heart and brain, a lot like a diver getting the bends.
A swollen fish cannot swim back down. That is why anglers now use devices that return it to depth.

description:
What if a fish was hauled up from deep water too fast?
The gas in its body expands, pushing its stomach out and bulging its eyes, a condition called barotrauma.
